title: Superficial Beliefs in LLM Decision-Making
abstract: arXiv:2606.11016v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We ask whether large language models (LLMs) merely imitate rationales when choosing between two options, or whether their choices reflect a systematic underlying decision structure. Using synthetic binary decision settings in which models choose between profiles defined by graded attributes, we compare the attribute a model says mattered most with the attribute that best explains its choice under a behavioural model fit to prior decisions. The behavioural model predicts held-out choices well, showing that model behaviour is systematically related to the visible attributes rather than being random. However, direct self-reports and a separate score-based judge recover the behaviourally inferred driver only partially. The resulting picture is neither one of arbitrary behaviour nor one of fully articulated belief - outputs are structured enough to support prediction, but explicit reasons track the recovered driver only imperfectly. translated_title: 大语言模型决策中的表层信念
translated_abstract: 我们探究大语言模型在两个选项之间做出选择时，是仅仅在模仿理由，还是其选择反映了某种系统性的底层决策结构。我们使用合成的二元决策场景，让模型在由分级属性定义的不同画像之间进行选择，并将模型声称最重要的属性与在基于先前决策拟合的行为模型下最能解释其选择的属性进行比较。行为模型能够很好地预测保留的测试选择，这表明模型行为与可见属性之间存在系统性关联，而非随机行为。然而，直接的自我报告和基于评分的独立评判机制只能部分恢复行为推断出的驱动因素。由此得出的图景既非任意行为，也非完全清晰表达的信念——输出结果具有足够的结构性以支持预测，但明确的理由陈述只能不完全地追踪恢复出的驱动因素。
tldr: 该研究通过行为模型分析发现，大语言模型的二元选择行为具有可预测的系统性结构，但其自我报告和评分评判所给出的明确理由只能部分反映真正的决策驱动因素。
en_tdlr: The study reveals that LLM binary decision-making behavior is systematically structured and well-predicted by behavioral models, yet their explicitly stated reasons—whether self-reports or score-based judgments—only partially reflect the true underlying decision drivers.
